tables_files: .dohc/engine/engine.db (renamed text file row, preserving stable objectId)
txn_ack_boundary: engine-side rename commits BEFORE the caller attempts the disk move; success is only final once the caller reports ok=true — the finisher contract makes the CALLER own the atomic pairing with the actual fs rename
ordering_idempotency: best-effort, not idempotent (a second call for the same pair after a completed rename sees toPath already tracked and falls back to no-op); rollback retries via enqueueResult, logging (not throwing) on rollback failure
security_class: workspace-scoped; preserves the linked-chat rail's stable object identity across the rename

io_contract: task:()=>Promise<{fastForwardedPaths,commitFetchCursor?}> -> same T | rejects; runs the caller's push/pull task, then materializes every fast-forwarded path to disk (deletes directly; writes read the fresh snapshot from the store) with expected-event suppression so the watcher never re-journals sync writes; ONLY THEN calls result.commitFetchCursor() — a materialization failure leaves the cursor uncommitted so the next pass re-fetches and retries the same ops
tables_files: .dohc/engine/engine.db (text table reads) + workspace files (materialized writes/deletes) + the relay fetch-cursor record (committed last)
txn_ack_boundary: the data-safety boundary for cloud sync — commitFetchCursor is the durability point, deliberately sequenced AFTER disk materialization succeeds, never before
ordering_idempotency: serialized on the chain (shared with local batch capture and version ops — sync can never interleave mid-version-switch); retryable — an uncommitted cursor makes the next pass safely reprocess the same paths
security_class: workspace-scoped; policy-filtered by the relay's own share/workspace scoping upstream

callers: tests; IPC handlers needing a synchronous "everything captured so far" guarantee
io_contract: void -> Promise<void>; resolves once everything enqueued SO FAR has been captured (does not block new enqueues that happen after the await starts)
txn_ack_boundary: chain-drain — the chain itself never rejects (errors caught+logged per task), so flush() cannot fail
ordering_idempotency: idempotent

io_contract: void -> Promise<void>; sets stopped=true (refuses NEW enqueue/enqueueResult calls — enqueueResult rejects immediately with "shutting down"), awaits everything already enqueued, then closes the SQLite handles for stores THIS capture instance created (an injected store, from tests, is left open — owned by its creator)
txn_ack_boundary: resolves only after every already-enqueued task (including the final pre-quit batch) has run and store handles are released — the guarantee workspaceActivity.stopAll's process-exit safety depends on
ordering_idempotency: idempotent (repeated stop() calls: stopped stays true, chain already resolved, close() called again on an already-closed store)

callers: materialize() (every version switch/merge/restore/rename/relay-sync write path), openYDocSession settle writer
io_contract: every materialization write/delete first calls assertEngineWritablePath (path must validateUserWritePath-normalize; protected writes must target a secret-classified path and nothing else; non-protected writes must NOT be secret-classified and must be policy-tracked); the disk writer walks up to the nearest EXISTING ancestor to confirm containment BEFORE mkdir, re-checks containment AFTER mkdir, and refuses a symlink LEAF before writeFile/rm
txn_ack_boundary: none atomic — the 3 checks (nearest-ancestor, post-mkdir, leaf-not-symlink) are sequential; a TOCTOU window exists between checks and the actual write (accepted given single-user-writable, not adversarial-multi-tenant)
ordering_idempotency: idempotent (repeated writes of the same content are a no-op upstream via writeIfChanged; the containment checks are stateless per call)
security_class: workspace-scoped; symlink-escape defense is the primary security contract — a rogue symlink anywhere in the ancestor chain or at the leaf must never redirect an engine write outside the workspace root

callers: reconcile() (capture-start-reconciliation, and every version op that reconciles disk into a version)
io_contract: void -> ReconcileScan{files,failedPaths}; tries a native workspace-kernel sidecar binary (handshake protocol-version+capability check, then kernel.scan) FIRST unless DOHC_KERNEL_SIDECAR=0 or the kernel is disabled-for-process; a kernel result is fully re-validated (safe normalized relative paths, finite non-negative sizes, hex sha256, string mediaType) INSIDE the try so a malformed-but-valid RPC response falls back rather than being trusted; ANY kernel failure falls back to the tolerant TS scan and increments a process-wide failure counter that permanently disables the kernel after WORKSPACE_KERNEL_FAILURE_DISABLE_THRESHOLD (3) consecutive failures
tables_files: reads the entire workspace tree (kernel sidecar or TS fallback); no engine.db access itself
txn_ack_boundary: none (pure scan, no writes); its failedPaths output feeds the TS-CONFIRMED delete gate downstream so an incomplete/degraded scan can never itself authorize a delete
ordering_idempotency: idempotent scan; the disable-after-3-failures counter is process-lifetime state, not per-call
security_class: workspace-scoped; a wrong-but-schema-valid kernel result is defended against by full re-validation plus the downstream TS-confirmed delete gate (fail-open-safe design)

callers: capture-start-reconciliation; createVersion/switchVersion/compareVersions/mergeVersionIntoMain (each reconciles the active/from version's disk state before its own operation)
io_contract: (engine,versionId,policy,metadata,scan?) -> void | throws (scan failure throws unless a pre-pinned scan was supplied, whose failedPaths are tolerated and reported by the caller); secret paths capture into the encrypted store; policy-untracked paths retire from engine state without touching disk; everything else writes-if-changed or retires if absent/untracked-content; retires any engine-tracked path NOT seen in the scan ONLY after a direct lstat CONFIRMS genuine absence (ENOENT/ENOTDIR) — an unreadable-but-present path, or a path under a scan-failed directory, is never retired (the false-delete defense for a default-on, possibly-incomplete kernel scan)
txn_ack_boundary: per-path, not whole-pass — no single commit boundary; a crash mid-pass leaves partial reconciliation, self-healed by the NEXT reconcile (idempotent equality-gated writes)
ordering_idempotency: idempotent by construction (content-equality no-op rule + confirmed-absence delete gate); safe to re-run from any partial state
security_class: workspace-scoped; the TS-confirmed delete gate is the core safety invariant preventing an incomplete disk listing from ever causing data loss
